A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WARD and FARAD. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original FARAD experiments, including baseline comparisons, watermark detection, text-quality evaluation, and robustness analyses in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline evaluations with realistic retrieval and a larger retrieved-document configuration.

M1.justification: WARD's watermarking, question generation, response aggregation, duplicate filtering, and detection procedure remain unchanged. The newly specified watermarking model and retrieval implementation clarify existing experiments; proposed future extensions are not implemented method changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate FARAD-Easy and FARAD-Hard, including idealized and realistic retrieval and existing defense scenarios. The additional comparisons and larger context configuration remain within this coverage. Other languages, domains, and human-written data are only future directions.

E2.justification: Section 5.3 adds FACTS, SIB, and AAG to the previously WARD-only realistic-retrieval experiment under FARAD-Hard and Def-P. The comparator set in the main experiment remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix C.1 extends the retrieved-document configurations from k = 3, 4, 5 to k = 10, switching to Claude 3 Haiku because of GPT-3.5's context limit. Existing dataset sampling, default settings, and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a larger-context robustness check, examines whether realistic retrieval changes baseline competitiveness, and translates query efficiency into estimated API costs. Existing watermark, dropout, MEMFREE, and threshold analyses are retained after moving from Appendix A to C.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds and retain the same statistical detection test and uncertainty-display practices. v2 does not report additional runs or a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure; numerical changes to Figure 9's bands concern results.

E6.justification: v2 adds realistic-retrieval results reporting 100% false positives for FACTS and 100% true negatives for SIB/AAG, and reports 100% accuracy in the new k = 10 configuration. Appendix D estimates $0.63 for 100 GPT-3.5 queries. Tables 1–2 remain unchanged; Figure 9 retains its mean curves with small band updates.

T1.justification: The RAG-DI definition, watermark z-score, green-token bound in Equations 1–2, and associated reasoning remain unchanged. No theorem, proof, or revised formal guarantee is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: formalizing RAG-DI, introducing FARAD and baselines, and demonstrating WARD's statistical guarantees, accuracy, efficiency, and robustness. Condensed wording and additional supporting checks do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendices A, D, and E substantially expand practical interpretation and applicability discussion: legal enforcement, auditing costs, dataset-size constraints, synthetic-document realism, and advanced countermeasures. v2 explicitly leaves full-paraphrasing defenses unevaluated while introducing an argument that their deployment would be costly.

D1.justification: v2 adds code and FARAD access information, an MIT-license statement, and descriptions of experiment configurations and reproduction instructions. It identifies Llama3.1-8B as the watermarking model and specifies ideal retrieval ordering and random document selection in Appendix B.2, substantially improving reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands positioning around data provenance, copyright disputes, and opt-out mechanisms, citing works and initiatives such as Longpre et al., Balan et al., C2PA, and SpawningAI. v2 also adds Jin et al. for retrieval settings and removes Sablayrolles et al.; publication updates to retained references are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the abstract and several passages, updates publication and author information, and adds ethics and reproducibility statements. Appendices are reorganized around new motivation, efficiency, and future-work sections, while the main section sequence and most existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables are retained. Figure 9's queries-per-document legend is sorted numerically with corresponding color reassignment; Table 1 labels and spacing are adjusted, and several displays are resized or repositioned. There is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies previously underspecified implementation details, provides code/data access information, and strengthens validation with targeted retrieval and larger-context checks. These improve reproducibility and assessment of practical use. The gains remain limited: broader generalization is still untested, and the added cost and countermeasure-feasibility arguments are estimates or discussion rather than comprehensive validation.
